correctness.rationale: For every even b>=4 and integer m>=1, a least-differing-digit argument gives an exact zero cosine factor and orthonormality of spectral and finite prefix matrices, including half-integer frequencies. Cylinder conditioning gives a diagonal Fourier product times a unitary matrix, proving each principal cosine; monotonicity gives a sharp minimum and projector gap. Digit coupling proves the singular-continuous limit with explicit Lipschitz rate, and direct convergent-product expansions prove the base and level asymptotics. The packaged deterministic checker passed 3,446 tests; no infinite claim depends on the finite test range.

value.rationale: The natural finite spatial-digit and canonical Fourier approximants have distinct Hilbert-space geometries even though they approximate the same fractal space. Their complete principal-angle law yields exact, sharp finite-level conversion bounds. The limiting angle spectrum is a non-atomic singular Cantor pushforward and the uniform transversality improves at a precisely quantified rate with the base. These are structural approximation invariants not a trivial scalar test or arbitrary numerical slice; downstream convergence estimates are not claimed.
